findings.detail: The Windows memory-lock portability change modified product code without updating the current slice record in the first candidate. The SLICE-PREP-2 row now names the code, tests and review record that cover this work before landing.

Four budgeted recovery-resume tests expected secure descriptor-relative evidence reads on Windows even though compatibility and task-acceptance documents explicitly return unsupported_platform there. The tests now use the existing SECURE_DESCRIPTOR_READS gate, matching the other resume tests and keeping unsupported behavior as skipped rather than failed.

Task-state projection excluded POSIX absolute artifact paths but accepted Windows drive and UNC paths, so read_input appeared in both absolute trace/session references and inflated the dependency prompt. Projection now rejects Windows absolute/drive references as non-workspace evidence, with a regression test for D:\ paths.

landing_sign_off.scope: Landing this exact medium-risk cross-platform lock candidate on main; no tag, Release, package upload or real provider run.

why: Windows CI imports failed because pocketchat.memory imported POSIX fcntl eagerly. After that was fixed, Windows exposed one task-state portability defect and four tests that contradicted the documented unsupported recovery-reader boundary.
not_doing: No memory format change, CLI/API change, provider call, release publication, package upload or workflow scope expansion.
diff_walk: pocketchat/memory.py: load lock backends lazily, map lock contention to MemoryError, track acquisition explicitly and unlock only a held lock.
pocketchat/task_state.py: keep projected trace/session references workspace-relative on both POSIX and Windows.

tests/test_memory.py, tests/test_task_state.py, tests/test_task_cli_resume.py and tests/test_task_exec.py: cover lock backends, Windows absolute artifact exclusion and the secure-reader skip contract.
CHANGELOG.md and docs/slice-queue.md: record the delivered portability behavior in the existing SLICE-PREP-2 evidence boundary.
static_checks: Windows calls msvcrt.locking with LK_NBLCK and LK_UNLCK; POSIX retains non-blocking flock behavior.
EACCES/EAGAIN lock contention remains the memory_store_is_busy path and failed acquisition is not unlocked.
Task-state artifact evidence excludes POSIX absolute, Windows drive and UNC paths.
Recovery resume tests requiring descriptor-relative evidence are skipped where SECURE_DESCRIPTOR_READS is false.
red_green: The no-fcntl import test failed with ModuleNotFoundError before lazy imports and passed after them.
The fake Windows lock test failed because the backend helper did not exist, then passed with the expected LK_NBLCK/LK_UNLCK calls.
The Windows absolute artifact projection test exposed trace/session keys before the fix and passed after portable absolute detection.
The first exact-SHA CI run reproduced four unsupported recovery failures and one Windows task-state prompt failure before the final fixes.
review_notes: The completed fresh-context review reported F1; exact-SHA CI then exposed F2 and F3. All three were reproduced and fixed with focused regressions before the second candidate.
gaps: The second exact-SHA CI run is pending; Windows recovery/acceptance support remains intentionally unverified and skipped.
